title: Amanah gold-standard label set v0.1
description: One labeller's output over one corpus, produced under LABELLING.md v0.1. This is the ground truth against which extraction is measured, so it is deliberately a separate artefact from SCHEMA.json: a label is what a human decided, not what a model returned. Labels carry no confidence, because a labeller who is unsure resolves it under section 5 of the protocol rather than recording a probability.

corpus.description: Identifier of the corpus file these labels apply to. Must match the corpus file's own 'corpus' field, so labels cannot be scored against the wrong text.

labeller.description: Opaque labeller identifier, e.g. 'A'. Never a name. Kept because where a second labeller exists (section 5b), agreement is reported before resolution and the two passes have to stay distinguishable.

protocol_version.description: Version of LABELLING.md the labeller worked under. A protocol change invalidates agreement figures in the same way a prompt change invalidates extraction metrics.

resolved.description: True when this set is the post-resolution gold standard, rather than one labeller's independent pass. Only a resolved set may be used as ground truth by score.mjs; agreement.mjs refuses to compare two resolved sets, because agreement is meaningless after resolution.

redacted.description: True when the quoted report text has been stripped for publication under a data use agreement that forbids redistributing the corpus. Spans, categories, intervals, flags and text_sha256 are all kept, and labels.mjs derives every quote from the reader's own rebuilt corpus. Redaction is all or nothing: a set marked redacted that still carries quoted text is rejected. Produced by redact.mjs. See LABELLING.md section 8a.

labelling.description: How this gold standard was made. Required on a resolved set, and printed by score.mjs above every metrics table. A metric is not independent of the ground truth it was scored against, in the same way no extraction metric is independent of the model that produced it. Section 5c.

labellers.description: How many people labelled. Under section 5a this is 1.

agreement.description: reported: inter-annotator agreement was measured on a subset and published (5b). not_measured: nothing was measured. intra_rater_only: the same person relabelled a subset blind, which measures consistency and NOT whether the protocol is unambiguous to somebody else (5a).

intra_rater_kappa.description: Cohen's kappa from the blind relabel under 5a. Never presented as inter-annotator agreement.

inter_rater_kappa.description: Cohen's kappa between two labellers under 5b. Null under 5a, and it must stay null rather than being filled with the intra-rater figure.

labels.description: One entry per report. Every report in the corpus must appear, including reports with no recommendation. A missing report is an incomplete label set, not an empty one, and the two must never be confused.

span.description: Character offset [start, end) into the report text. Section 4 requires round-trip: text.slice(start, end) must equal the verbatim string exactly, or the label is invalid and is rejected by labels.mjs.

report_id.description: Must exist in the corpus file.

text_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the report text as labelled. Binds spans to exact characters: if the corpus text is later normalised, whitespace-fixed or re-extracted, every offset silently moves and the labels become wrong while still looking valid. Checked on load.

date_found.description: The report's own date. Section 4: where several dates appear, take the study date. Null where none is determinable, never today's date.

recommendations.description: Zero or more recommendation instances. An empty array is a positive assertion that this report contains no follow-up recommendation, and such reports are how the false-positive rate is measured. Section 1 targets at least 60% of the set.

note.description: Labeller's note on a judgement call. Where a note records a decision not covered by the protocol, it should also be appended to section 7 as a precedent.

recommendation_verbatim.description: Copied exactly as printed, including typographical errors. Section 4: do not tidy. Required on a normal label set and ABSENT on a redacted one, where labels.mjs derives it from the span. That conditional requirement is enforced by the loader rather than by this schema, because a set marked redacted must be rejected for carrying the field at all, which is the opposite of a required check.

equivalent_spans.description: Other places the SAME sentence appears in the report. Section 7.6: a recommendation stated twice is one instance, labelled from the impression, so an extractor quoting the findings copy has found the same duty and must not be scored as a fabrication. The canonical recommendation_span stays the one thing the verification screen highlights and the prepared summary quotes; these are consulted only when matching. Derived by label-server.mjs rather than entered by hand, and the loader rejects any span whose text differs from the canonical one, so this cannot become a licence to make the gold standard match anything. Absent when the sentence appears once, which is the common case.

finding.description: Controlled category. The enum is not repeated here: labels.mjs validates against FINDING_CATEGORIES exported by extract.mjs, so the vocabulary has one definition rather than three.

action.description: Validated against ACTIONS exported by extract.mjs.

anatomy.description: Only where the report is specific. Section 4: 'nodule in the lung' is null, not lung.unspecified.

interval.description: Only when stated. Section 4: a range such as '6-12 months' is null with the range kept in interval_verbatim, and a guideline reference such as 'as per Fleischner' is null.

negated.description: Section 4: 'No further imaging required' is a labelled instance with negated true, not an empty set. It is evidence for the not_indicated terminal state.
